Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing the star key followed by one on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics' Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer; David Harlan, Chief Strategy Officer; Karen Ruiz, Chief Marketing Officer; and Thomas Lee, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results could differ materially due to various risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of these risks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a solid performance in the second quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense systems, missiles, space, and commercial aviation. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Let me start with one of our most critical leading indicators: backlog growth. As everyone knows, in our sector, backlog provides high-confidence visibility into future revenues from funded orders under firm fixed-price, cost-plus, or time-and-materials contracts yet to be executed—it's essential for predictable cash flow and multi-year program stability. I'm pleased to report that our total backlog at quarter-end stood at $58.7 billion, up $5.2 billion sequentially from Q1's $53.5 billion, marking a robust 9.7% quarter-over-quarter increase. Year-over-year, it's surged by $14.1 billion, or 31.7%, from $44.6 billion in Q2 last year—the strongest quarterly expansion since Q4 FY2021 during the initial low-rate initial production for our NextGen Air Dominance platform. Breaking it down by segment highlights our diversification: Defense Systems, at 72% of backlog with $42.3 billion, grew $4.1 billion or 10.7% quarter-over-quarter and 35.2% year-over-year, driven by a $2.8 billion award modification for Lot 16 F-35 Lightning II wing production amid the program's momentum with over 1,000 jets delivered industry-wide, plus a $1.2 billion foreign military sales contract for hypersonic boost-glide vehicle boosters to a NATO ally responding to Eastern European tensions. Missiles & Precision Weapons, 15% of backlog at $8.8 billion, increased $0.8 billion or 10% quarter-over-quarter and 28.4% year-over-year, thanks to bookings for our Extended Range Anti-Ship Missile akin to the LRASM family, ramping to support U.S. Navy Pacific deterrence, with book-to-bill at 1.4x against our 1.1x-1.2x target. Space & Advanced Systems, 8% at $4.7 billion, rose $0.3 billion or 6.8% quarter-over-quarter and 22.1% year-over-year, featuring a $450 million NASA contract for Orion spacecraft propulsion modules positioning us against Blue Origin and SpaceX in Artemis, and initial funding for our proliferated low-Earth orbit satellite constellation demo under the Space Development Agency's Tranche 2 Transport Layer. Commercial Aviation, 5% at $2.9 billion, edged up $0.1 billion or 3.6% quarter-over-quarter but held flat year-over-year amid supply chain challenges, with narrowbody aftermarket orders for CFM LEAP-compatible nacelles stabilizing post-737 MAX delays. Overall book-to-bill was 1.35x, with Defense at 1.5x, even as shipments rose 12% year-over-year. Funded backlog is 68%, or $40 billion, for near-term visibility, with $18.7 billion unfunded aligning with DoD patterns. Regionally, U.S. DoD drove 62% of new awards under the FY2024 NDAA's $886 billion topline up 4.1%, emphasizing integrated air-and-missile defense, while international backlog leaped 42% year-over-year to $19.2 billion from Middle East Patriot PAC-3 MSE equivalents hedging Iranian proxies and Asia-Pacific AUKUS hypersonics and GCAP tech transfers to Japan and Australia. We're sustaining this with $1.2 billion in digital engineering twins using Siemens NX and ANSYS for 6x faster F-35 Lot 18 tooling, cutting sole-source delays 25%, plus a new 500,000 sq ft Huntsville facility for solid rocket motors to counter ammonium perchlorate inflation under export controls. We expect 8-10% backlog growth in H2 FY2024 to $63-65 billion by year-end, assuming steady Ukraine and Israel aid, though risks like sequestration or 787 titanium issues linger—but our 24-month labor stability edges us over peers.

Shifting to our capital deployment strategy, which is central to shareholder value in this landscape. We operate across fixed-wing like F-35 sustainment and NGAD pursuits, rotary-wing and unmanned akin to V-280 Valor and MQ-Next drones, space and missile defense with hypersonic glide vehicles and directed energy, and commercial supporting narrowbody re-engining amid Boeing and Airbus ramps. Our approach is disciplined: maintain investment-grade strength with net leverage below 2.0x EBITDA—now at 1.6x, backed by $12.5 billion liquidity and $4.2 billion cash equivalents. We prioritize organic reinvestment at 4-5% of revenues for capacity and IRAD, then dividends—recently raised 8% to $1.12 annual, yielding 1.6% with payout ratio under 40%—share repurchases under our $2 billion authorization, executing $450 million in Q2 at average $285/share, and tuck-in acquisitions like last year's $650 million autonomy software bolt-on enhancing CCA swarming. M&A targets focus on adjacencies in hypersonics and space PNT, with pipeline at $5-7 billion deployable opportunistically, always preserving $10 billion dry powder for downturns.

On the defense budget outlook and its impact, geopolitical drivers like Russia's Ukraine invasion, China's Indo-Pacific moves, and Iran's proxies sustain global spending—SIPRI notes $2.44 trillion in 2023, up 6.8% real terms, the steepest since the Cold War, per the U.S. National Defense Strategy. U.S. FY2025 NDAA at $895 billion, up 4.1% from FY2024's $860 billion plus $95 billion supplemental for Ukraine, Israel, and deterrence. Procurement up 5.2% to $168 billion with $12.5 billion air-launched munitions like JASSM-ER, LRASM, our HGV for AGM-183A; RDT&E up 6.8% to $145 billion on hypersonics ($12B+), NGAD ($2.5B), CCA ($3.2B) aligning with our Penetrator-VI digital twins using AI/ML MBSE; O&M steady at $287 billion for F-35 sustainment where our ALIS-to-ODIN modules grab 18% share. OCO embedded adds $50 billion buffer. Europe/NATO at $380 billion up 12%, Poland $40B including our Riptide missiles, Germany €100B for F-35; Indo-Pacific AUKUS $200B+, Japan $320B for hypersonics/CCAs, positioning us for $4-6B FMS; Middle East GCC $120B up 8%, Saudi $75B for Stormbreaker munitions. For us, funded backlog hits $128 billion up 14% YoY, book-to-bill 1.25x from $2.7B CCA Phase 2 and $1.8B HGV wins, international 28% of backlog. FY2024 guidance raised: revenue $27.5-29.0B, margins 11.8-12.2%, EPS $8.45-8.75; FY2025 7-9% organic, Aeronautics +10%, Missiles +12%, Space +8%. Pillars: $1.2B IRAD for digital engineering cutting NGAD cycles 35%, Ghostwing CCA 500+ hours; supply chain 85% dual-sourced, 98% on-time; LRIP stability for $10B+ JADC2. Risks like CRs or caps, but 65% multi-year fixed-price, 115% cash conversion, $4.2B FCF intact.

Major new contract awards have been exceptional, securing $6.2 billion—up 28% YoY, strongest since JASSM ramp, lifting backlog to $48.7 billion, 62% funded, book-to-bill 1.35x above 1.1x target for mid-teens growth through FY25-29 FYDP. U.S. Air Force $2.1B IDIQ for Block III LRASM full-rate production with AI seeker for sub-3m CEP in GPS-denied, LRIP deliveries ahead for Super Hornets/B-1Bs, Pacific deterrence vs A2/AD. U.S. Army $1.4B OTA for FLRAWS prototype, multi-mode GaN AESA seeker, TRL 8 at Yuma, 40% logistics cut for MDO. FMS 35% of bookings: $1.3B Saudi PAC-3 MSE with hypersonic software vs Houthi drones; $650M NATO/UK CCA demonstrators with EagleEye AI, 95% swarm success Black Dart. Space: $450M SDA Tranche 2 36 ocomm sats pLEO; $250M MDA HELIOS 300kW laser Milestone B from USS Portland to fixed hypersonic intercept. Tailwinds: 12% global spending rise, $886B U.S.; digital first shortens bids 25%, NGAD integrator; Middle East 18% backlog, APAC 40%. Q3 bookings $3-4B, year 1.2x+; investing in Huntsville expansion, pending autonomy M&A.

Program margins and cost performance showed solid execution in our A&D segment at $4.2B revenue up 8% YoY, margins up 120bps to 12.8%—best Q3 in five years vs industry 10-11%, EBITDA 15.4%, cash conversion 105%. Fixed-Wing 42% revenue, margins 11.2% up from 9.8% on ViperStrike F-35A Lot 16 (28 ships, 95% rate, unit costs -7% via digital twins/auto composites), NGAD engine dev -2.5% mitigated by GE/P&W shares $250M cap; FMS Japan/Australia $1.1B at 13%. Integrated Defense 35%, 14.7% up 250bps on hypersonic interceptor 18% margins $800M LRIP, $45M savings additive ti nozzles -22% scrap/9mo leads; Patriot GEM-T inflation offset clauses $30M YTD recover, Middle East FMS 16%. Sustainment 23%, 18.5% up 80bps, $950M PBL F-16/18 92%+ availability, AI preempts $28M failures, AR repairs +15% productivity, Europe Typhoon $200M 20%. Holistic: 92% EVMS CPI 1.05>0.98, $120M YTD savings—supply 45% ti/rare earths dual US/Aus -60% spot, labor 30% ZBB ABC -8% G&A, tech 25% $150M Industry 4.0 3:1 ROI. Headwinds 5-7% forgings/10% labor hedged 65% fixed-price. U.S. 72% $52B backlog 15% up, int'l 28% 16% premium. Outlook Q4 13.0-13.5%, FY 12.5% +150bps consensus, 10% 2025 growth "Margin First" digital/supplier/PBL for 5% CAGR $900B market.

For revenue and earnings guidance by segment, Aeronautics 45% at $14.0-14.5B, +9% YoY on F-35 ramps/margins 10.8%; Missiles & Fire Control 30% $9.3-9.7B +14% hypersonics/Patriot 13.8%; Space 20% $6.0-6.3B +10% SDA/NSSL 14.2%; Commercial 5% $1.2-1.3B stabilizing aftermarket 11.5%.

Full-year updated guidance reflects Q3 strength: prior revenue $29.5-30.5B, EPS $13.50-14.50, margins 11.0-11.5%; now revenue $31.0-32.0B +8-10% midpoint, organic 12% Missiles/Space; margins 11.8-12.3% +70bps fixed-fee/labor digital -22% ECO; EPS $15.00-16.00 +$1.25 mid favorable adjusts; CFO $3.8-4.2B, FCF $3.2-3.6B for $1.2B repurchases/1.8% dividend. Aeronautics $14.2-14.7B F-35 160 jets TR-3 $2.1B MBSE -30% validation; Missiles $9.5-10.0B 15% JASSM/Patriot ARRW $8B 1.4x 13.5-14.0%; Space $7.3-7.5B Tranche 2 14% AM SRM -9mo int'l +25%; U.S. 72% NDAA $900B, int'l 22% +14% F-35/AUKUS, comm 6% Starship MRO. Backlog $52B 1.7x vis 40% fixed, $1.1B IRAD DEW/C4ISR JADC2; risks CRs/labor/forex but 60% fixed defense tilt.

Strategic priorities and outlook: Q3 strong but framing Q4/FY2024/FY2025. Priorities: Defense modernization—NGAD LRIP H1'25 $1.2B, hypersonics ARRW/HAWC $450M Mach5+, DEW 300kW 95% uptime DDG-51; Europe €320M Typhoon, Saudi $600M GEM-T +25% ramp. Commercial resilience 15% YoY $650M 777X 110%, $250M capex 777-10, HyPoint H2 30% emissions cut. Space NovaSat 42 sats <1ns PNT $800M NSSL 15 launches, AUKUS/India. Digital MBSE Palantir -22% F-35 ECO, 8.5% rev $2.4B IRAD MQ-Next 5:1 sims. Q4 rev $2.9-3.0B +10-13% EPS $2.05-2.15; FY24 $11.5-11.7B +11% EPS $7.80-8.00 FCF $1.4B 125%NI Defense 15.5%/Space13.8%/Comm11.2%; FY25 $12.8-13.2B +11-14% 20% Defense. Risks Boeing/ti but dual-source/inventory; upside JASSM recompetes. Aligned $10T DoD pipeline/12k acft/space15%CAGR, ROIC 18% '26.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NextGen Air Dominance program and its potential to drive multi-year growth. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q2, we reported revenue of $7.6 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $3.45. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $4.8 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at the updated levels shared earlier. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include:
Gross Margin: 12.5%
Operating Income: $1.15 billion
Free Cash Flow: $950 million

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 lots and hypersonic boosters. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Specifically, our new Huntsville facility is yielding 20% throughput gains, and digital twins have slashed qualification times across missile programs.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Raj. On the technology front, we're making significant strides in our next-generation propulsion systems, including adaptive cycle engines for NGAD and solid rocket motors with additive manufacturing. We anticipate these advancements will give us a competitive edge in the years to come. More specifically, our Ghostwing CCA has logged over 500 flight hours, and AI-driven seekers are achieving breakthrough accuracy in contested environments.

David Harlan:
Thank you, Lisa. From a strategic perspective, we are actively evaluating potential acquisitions that would complement our existing portfolio and expand our market reach, such as recent autonomy software deals. We are also focused on developing new business models that will allow us to capture emerging opportunities. For instance, partnerships under AUKUS Pillar II for hypersonics and JADC2 interoperability are unlocking billions in international pursuits.

Karen Ruiz:
Thank you, David. From a marketing perspective, we are seeing great success with our new branding campaign emphasizing "Digital First Defense," which is resonating well with DoD and allied procurement teams. We are also leveraging digital channels to reach new customers and increase brand awareness. The results are a 25% uptick in web inquiries and stronger positioning in GCAP and Tempest bids.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth drivers, especially international?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Certainly, John. The international piece, now 33% of backlog at $19.2 billion up 42% YoY, is fueled by FMS urgency—Middle East hedging with PAC-3 equivalents, Asia-Pacific accelerating AUKUS hypersonics. Combined with DoD NDAA momentum, this gives us unmatched visibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, I'm curious about your capital deployment priorities amid high valuations?

Michael Reynolds:
Emily, we stick to our framework: balance sheet first at <2x leverage, then organic capex/IRAD, dividends up 8%, $450M Q2 buybacks. M&A opportunistic for tech adjacencies, $5-7B pipeline with $10B powder ensures flexibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Regarding the defense budget outlook and any FY25 risks?

Lisa Chen:
David, FY25 NDAA $895B looks solid with RDT&E emphasis on NGAD/CCA/hypersonics directly funding our pipeline. CR delays possible but our classified $15B backlog and multi-year contracts buffer that.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Gonzalez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Gonzalez:
Question about updated full-year guidance assumptions?

David Harlan:
Laura, the raise assumes 12% organic in high-growth segments, backlog conversion, margin tailwinds from learning curves/digital efficiencies. Supply chain derisked, forex hedged—positions us for 7-9% FY25 organic too.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
